author: Lucas Fernandez - World Editor
title: Australia to Introduce Law Forcing Tech Giants to Pay for Journalism
text:
Concurrently, the federal government moved to introduce high-stakes media bargaining legislation aimed at forcing tech platforms to pay for local journalism.
The Icac Testimony and Political Fallout Opposition figures have since insisted that staff members must strictly adhere to authorized communication channels and policy positions, maintaining that unauthorized remarks do not represent the broader Coalition platform.
Legislative Push for Tech Platform Payments Away from the corruption inquiry, the federal government confirmed it will introduce mandatory legislation compelling major technology companies to pay for Australian journalism. The parliamentary introduction follows a series of eleventh-hour negotiations and a formal agreement reached with the Coalition.
Under the framework of the new bill, digital platforms must enter into a minimum of eight distinct commercial deals with news publishers if they wish to fully offset their statutory obligations. While tech giants retain the flexibility to enter fewer agreements and only partially offset their obligations, the framework deliberately introduces strong financial incentives to drive broad industry engagement.
Crucially, the legislation includes a 200% offset calculation for small and medium players. This mechanism provides a powerful incentive for tech firms to cut deals with regional media networks, culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) outlets, LGBTQI publications, and other independent community operators.
Opposition representatives noted that remarks made by Andrew at the National Press Club reflected personal views rather than established policy, emphasizing that the Coalition’s formal positions are developed through careful, deliberate internal processes.
Regional Media Impact and Economic Pressures The integration of strict bargaining rules marks a major shift for Australia’s media landscape, directly impacting regional newsrooms fighting to maintain operational viability against falling advertising revenues. Smaller publishers across remote and metropolitan jurisdictions stand to benefit significantly if tech platforms trigger the multi-deal offset thresholds.
Australia's New Rules Force Big Tech to Pay for News: A Game Changer for Journalism
